files.note: Read all 20 scripts against the tree: every node, python and vitest entry file exists, `check` chains the seven gates plus the memory tests, and `tokens` points at the real report script. Dependency names match the imports used by the src tree; no script is duplicated, stale or missing its file.

Read the package, lib, features, dependency and profile sections: Rust 1.90 floor, tray on by default, test-fakes kept out of release, local profile inherits release with thin LTO, and the Windows-only crates are pinned to the versions wry builds. No crate used by the files of this area is missing.

Checked the msvc branch: tauri-build runs without its own manifest, the segment-heap manifest is written to OUT_DIR and linked into every target, and the two failure points are build-time expect() calls that cannot fire at runtime.

Matched every window call in src/ (show, close, minimize, toggle-maximize, is-maximized, start-dragging, set-focus, unminimize, webview zoom) to a permission here, and checked the dialog plugin: only `open` is used, so allow-save is rightly absent. core:default covers the event listen calls.
The entry point only calls kolux_lib::run(); the release build keeps the console window hidden. Nothing in this file can panic or swallow an error.

The three resources resolve relative to src-tauri and all exist. The CSP is the one scripts/csp.test.mjs compares with vite.config.ts, and style-src is the only disabled injection. The empty updater pubkey is deliberate: release.mjs writes the real key per build and update.rs turns checks off when it is absent.

Traced every subcommand from parseArgs into lib.mjs: build, status, search, timeline, session, agent, card, record, items, resume, export. `record` hands detail and evidence straight to recordItem, whose missing redaction is reported against lib.mjs as S3-F05, and no command catches an error and then prints a success line.

Read the whole builder: build and its source readers, redact and keep, readGit, recordItem and readLedger, resumeMarkdown and exportMarkdown. Five defects are proved by the repro tests: the sessions guard does not cover the message query, redact misses the JSON form, readGit drops body lines after the first, recordItem never redacts, and the Next list numbers 1 then 3. search, timeline, status, findSession and listItems were also called on a probe database with empty, wildcard and quote input and returned sane results.

The five tests build a synthetic machine and never touch the real profile; all five pass today. They cover build, record plus rebuild, search, items and resume, but none covers a store with a different schema, a JSON-shaped secret, a multi-line commit body or the Next numbering, which is why the five repro tests sit in their own files.

Checked the dev server (fixed port 1420, strict, no screen clear, src-tauri ignored), the vendor-mark asset rule and the vitest include patterns. The repro tests were written under scripts/ because `scripts/**/*.test.mjs` is what this config picks up.
